decisions.executionNote: Establish elbow-up approach on each side; watches to white, pens to blue, cameras to red. Initial motion raises wrists and begins downward gripper orientation.
Approach left watch and rightmost camera from above on separate sides, gradually pitching grippers down; final alignment will use wrist views.
Lower toward the first watch and camera with small corrections; complete nearly vertical approach, leaving grippers open for visual alignment.
Align the jaws with the watch band and camera body, descend the last few centimeters, and close both grippers. Retention remains unconfirmed until lifting.
Lift both objects clear of the tabletop, keeping the jaws closed, then start moving toward the white watch basket and red camera basket.
Both objects are visibly retained. Replan with smaller increments after continuity rejection, tilting forward slightly to place over basket interiors without further large wrist reach.
Release the first watch and camera over their separate baskets, then lift and retract toward the remaining left watch and right camera.
Move above the second watch and second camera with vertical jaws, keeping clear of the three pens and the remaining right watch.
Use wrist-view offsets to center the second watch and camera, lower cautiously, close fully, and begin a short retention-check lift.
Lift to check retention. The camera appears pinched securely; the watch may have slipped to one side, so keep its lift vertical and inspect before transporting.
The second watch stayed on the table. Reopen and recenter lower over its band while carrying the visibly retained second camera toward the red basket.
Close around the centered watch band and lift vertically to verify; move the second camera slightly deeper into the red basket before releasing it.
Lift the second watch higher and carry it toward white. Approach the remaining right-side watch with the empty right gripper; both cameras are now visible inside red.
Carry the retained second watch over white while carefully lowering and closing around the last watch on the right side.
Release the second watch into white and withdraw the left wrist toward the black pen. Lift the last watch with the right arm before staging it at the center for left-side transfer.
The right watch remained on the table. Reopen and return lower over its band; simultaneously align the left jaws perpendicular to the horizontal black pen and descend.
Correct lateral wrist offsets, grasp the black pen near its barrel and the right watch around its band, then make a short vertical lift to check retention.
The pen appears retained; lift and carry toward blue. The right watch slipped and shifted backward on the table, so reopen and approach its new position lower.
The black pen stayed on the table, so return with open jaws for a lower grasp. Close around the now-centered right watch and lift vertically before any transfer.
Lower the centered black-pen grasp to the tabletop, close, and test lift. The right watch is visibly retained; carry it to a central staging area without crossing arms.
Lift and carry the black pen toward blue with jaws closed. Lower the retained right watch onto a clear central staging spot for a later left-arm pickup.
The pen slipped during lifting; leave it for a fresh grasp. Set the last watch down centrally and withdraw the right arm, while the left reorients for the watch transfer.
Approach the staged watch with the left arm as the right clears the center and aligns above its diagonal black pen. Keep both grasp axes nearly vertical.
Center and lower onto the staged watch band before closing. Bring the right gripper down toward the diagonal pen, leaving it open for a final wrist-view adjustment.
Allow the watch jaws time to finish closing before a short lift. Lower the right jaws the last 23 mm around the pen and close while holding position.
Recenter lower and slightly rearward on the staged watch because it appears to have slipped. Give the right pen grasp additional closure time, then lift only vertically to verify retention.
Carry the visibly retained right pen toward blue, keeping it closed. Complete watch closure, lift vertically, then start moving the left arm back into its own workspace toward white.
Both objects remain visibly held. Carry the final watch left toward white and the black pen toward the center blue basket, keeping the arms separated.
After the continuity stop, make only a small right-wrist adjustment and release the pen over blue rather than extending further. Bring the final watch over white.
Release the final watch into white; all watches and cameras are now in their assigned baskets. Retract the right arm and orient the left jaws across the remaining black pen.
Approach the remaining black pen with jaws perpendicular to its barrel. Begin returning the empty right arm toward its initial pose while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Lower and close around the left black pen without lifting during closure. Continue a gradual right-arm return, leaving it clear of the remaining left-side work.
The left jaws appear impeded at table level and slightly off center. Recenter by 6 mm with a small clearance lift, then reclose and dwell. Bring the right wrist near its origin.
Finish closing and lift the centered black pen vertically for a retention check. Complete the right arm's small final return to its starting pose.
The black pen remains fixed between the jaws during the lift. Carry it toward the blue basket with a slight forward tilt, keeping the right arm parked.
Shift the retained pen fully over the blue interior with small increments, lower slightly, and open to release. The white pen is the only object still on the table.
Both black pens are now visible in blue. Withdraw clear of them and align the open left gripper over the last white pen, with a vertical approach.
Lower the centered jaws to the white pen's barrel and close without lifting, allowing time for the small-diameter grasp to settle.
Finish closing around the white pen, then lift straight up for a retention check before moving to blue.
The white pen remains visibly fixed in the jaws. Carry it over the blue basket with the same gentle forward tilt used for the preceding pen.
Release the final white pen into blue, then retract the left wrist and start its smooth return toward origin. Keep both grippers open and let the sorted objects settle.
All objects are off the table and grouped in the three baskets. Continue the left arm's gradual return, with open jaws and clearance above the settled objects.
Complete the left wrist's return to its original position and orientation in small continuous steps. Both grippers remain open while the sorted baskets settle.
